doc.title: Fred Staton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 12, 2008

title: Advice on music careers and his grandchildren
summary: He would encourage a grandson to try music, but none of his family is in it; the last ten years are his highlight.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: It’s a tough business no matter what. If you had a grandson —
You have several. If they asked you about going into music as a career, what would your advice be?
I would encourage it. Sure. Yeah. Do what you feel comfortable with. If you feel comfortable with it, do it. But if you don’t feel comfortable, no, don’t force yourself.
Yeah. What do your grandkids do?

None of them are in music. None of them. My grandson is in educational — he’s a teacher in a public school. And I have four, four — yeah — four great grandchildren. None of them are interested in it, none of them. They come to see me perform from time to time, and they enjoy it. They’re not interested so far.
What was the — like the highlight of your musical endeavors? Has it been the last ten years as you’ve said?
Yeah. Because it was always a struggle.
